findings.title: Backup code can bypass password verification when combined with a dummy TOTP code
findings.body: Password verification is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is present (line 121), while the backup-code branch at line 131 is selected solely from credentials.backupCode and never validates totpCode. An attacker who obtains only one backup code can therefore call the credentials provider directly with any password, a non-empty dummy totpCode, and that backup code: the password check is bypassed and only the backup code is checked, turning a second factor into a single-factor login. Password verification must not depend on totpCode, or must be explicitly required in the backup-code branch as it is in the normal form flow.

findings.title: Backup-code comparison is case-sensitive while users are shown uppercase-style codes
findings.body: Setup generates codes with crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex') (lowercase a-f) in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts, but login only strips '-' before indexOf, and the input placeholder is 'XXXXX-XXXXX' suggesting uppercase entry. A user who transcribes or types a code in uppercase (e.g. 'ABC12-DEF34') will always get IncorrectBackupCode even though it is the correct code. The same case-sensitive pattern exists in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61. Normalize input with toLowerCase() (and trim) before comparison in both places.

findings.title: Single-use backup code can be replayed by concurrent login requests
findings.body: Authorize reads user.backupCodes, checks indexOf, then writes back the array with that entry nulled as a separate non-atomic update. Two concurrent authorize calls with the same backup code can both read the pre-consumption value, both pass the check, and both log in before either update lands, violating the documented 'each backup code can be used exactly once' guarantee. Consumption needs an atomic/transactional compare-and-update (or row locking) so only one request can claim a code.

findings.title: Parent is only notified of enabled 2FA if the user clicks the backup-codes Close button
findings.body: Previously handleEnable called onEnable() as soon as the enable request succeeded; now it only advances to DisplayBackupCodes, and onEnable() is invoked solely from the backup-codes-close button (line 269). If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (Dialog close control / onOpenChange, Escape, backdrop), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent settings page is never told, so the 2FA switch/state remains stale (showing disabled) until a reload and can invite a confusing re-setup attempt that the API rejects with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. Notify the parent on successful enable, or on any close from the DisplayBackupCodes step.

findings.title: No test exercises login or disable with a backup code, including single-use rejection
findings.body: The PR adds backup-code authentication to the credentials authorize flow and to the disable endpoint, but the only added e2e coverage downloads/copies the codes during setup; the file itself notes 'TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. Core security behavior — successful login with a valid code, rejection of a wrong code, rejection when reusing an already-consumed code, and disabling 2FA with a code — is unverified, so a regression in consumption/normalization would ship unnoticed.
